title: RFC 2046 §5.1.1 boundary collision check in sign()
description: boundary_from_content (sign.rs) derives the boundary from SHA-256 of content and then explicitly checks that the boundary does not appear as a substring of the content. The comment correctly explains the security reasoning (birthday-attack level collision resistance). A contributor might suggest removing the check as 'paranoid', but without it, any content that happens to contain the boundary string would produce a structurally broken MIME message that parsers reject silently or misparse.
close_reason: P3 opinion/style: no correctness issue, deferred.
